headline: 36% of regular students skipping HSC exams this year, a significant rise from last year's 29%
summary: An alarming 5.5 lakh regular students, out of 15 lakh registered, are not participating in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations, marking an unusual increase.
details: A staggering 36% of regular students are not participating in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations. This translates to approximately 5.5 lakh students out of 15 lakh who registered two years ago for the 2024-25 academic session.
This year's absenteeism rate is considered unusually high by education officials. Last year, the rate was just over 29%, indicating a nearly 7 percentage point increase in a single year.
The situation is particularly concerning for the Bangladesh Technical Education Board, where over 54% of regular students did not even fill out the examination forms this year.

While specific reasons for such a large number of dropouts within two years are unknown, an analysis by the Dhaka Education Board last year shed some light. It found that child marriage was the primary reason for absence for about 41% of students surveyed, alongside lack of preparation and poverty.

The trend of increasing absenteeism is not new; even after filling out forms, the number of absent students on the first day of exams has risen. This suggests students are disengaging from studies at various points after registration.

Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Hoque Milan stated that weaknesses are being identified, and necessary measures will be taken based on the information gathered. He expressed hope that such incidents would not occur in the future.
Across the nine general education boards, 33.04% of regular students are not taking the exam, up from 27% last year. For the Madrasa Education Board, this figure is 44.07%, an increase from 39%.
This year, a total of 12,70,583 regular and irregular candidates are appearing for the HSC and equivalent examinations. The exams are being held at 2,697 centers nationwide.

headline: Doctor jailed for not testifying in rape case
summary: A doctor has been sentenced to jail for failing to appear as a witness in a rape case.
details: A medical professional has been sentenced to imprisonment for failing to provide testimony in a rape case. This judicial action underscores the critical role of witnesses in ensuring justice.
The court emphasized the importance of cooperation from all parties, especially expert witnesses, to ensure fair and timely legal proceedings.
